title: The Crater That Killed the Dinosaurs Is 180 km Wide
description:
Unreal but true: a new real event every day at 5:48 pm (Riyadh).

About 66 million years ago, an asteroid or comet about 10 km wide hit what is now the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico. It left the Chicxulub crater, about 180 km wide (some studies argue for 200 km or even 300 km). Today the crater is still there, buried under about 1 km of younger rock, centred near the town of Chicxulub. The impact is widely accepted as the main cause of the mass extinction that ended the age of the dinosaurs.

The crater rim is drawn as a simple circle on a real map, and the counter is not in real time: the real crater formed in minutes.

Sources: NASA JPL, "A Smoking Gun for Dinosaur Extinction" (180 km crater, about 10 km impactor, buried under about 1 km of rock); NASA JPL Photojournal PIA01723 (Chicxulub crater, 180 to 300 km debated); Wikipedia, "Chicxulub crater" (180 to 200 km, about 66 million years ago, 21.4 N 89.5 W); HowStuffWorks, "Chicxulub Crater".
Animation drawn in code on a Natural Earth map; narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs).

Did you guess it? Tell me your number in the comments.
